solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Loose definition would be 'fancy-free'

definitions.meaning: loose here means not fixed or fastened to anything
fancy-free means not in love or committed to anyone, single

explanation.surface: A wry dictionary entry: the slack definition of 'fancy-free'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: something loose is not fastened, and a fancy-free person is not in a relationship.

clue.text: Only thumbs down from the corner

parts.note: a thumbs-down says 'no' to something offered as 'OK', so the phrase splits into NO and OK
a thumbs-down says 'no' to something offered as 'OK', so the phrase splits into NO and OK

explanation.surface: Someone in the corner of a room gives nothing but disapproving thumbs-down gestures.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue invites reading the letters as NO OK, a rejection, which is what a thumbs-down signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small recess or sheltered corner of a room.

clue.text: Sweet towards female taking charge

parts.note: towards means to, as in heading to a place
a charge is a fee paid for a service

explanation.surface: A woman takes charge, moving sweetly towards command.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee is a chewy confection, a kind of sweet in British usage (candy elsewhere).

clue.text: He doesn't accept money on the side

definitions.text: He doesn't accept money on the side

parts.words: He doesn't accept money on the side
parts.note: reads like someone refusing bribes or extra earnings, but means a player in a team (a side) who takes no pay

explanation.surface: An honest man refuses any money on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the side' suggests secret payments; it means playing on a sports team.
explanation.definitionFit: An unpaid sportsman playing for a team is a non-professional player.

clue.text: Awful die-hard, to start with, having a thick skin

indicators.note: to start with picks only the opening letter of the word hard
awful suggests something messed up, so the letters of die and one more are jumbled

explanation.surface: An awful die-hard who is thick-skinned about criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'die-hard' splits into two words: DIE is the anagram fodder with H from 'hard' to start with, and 'Awful' shuffles them.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's hide is its tough outer skin, especially a thick one.

clue.text: Risks many may take makes one see red

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a crossword shorthand for many
something that makes one see red angers one

explanation.surface: Many people may take risks that make others furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Dangers are hazards or perils, the things one risks.

clue.text: Expanding hole in tooth?

definitions.meaning: expanding means growing larger or plumper
a hole in a tooth is where a dentist's filling has come out

explanation.surface: A dental cavity that keeps getting bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: To be growing plumper is an idiom for expanding; and a lost dental plug leaves a cavity.

clue.text: A Pole in training to beat an Italian

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so the letters of a pole and in are rearranged

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: A Polish athlete in training hopes to beat an Italian rival.
explanation.definitionFit: A Neapolitan is a native of Naples, so an Italian person.

clue.text: Whence came the needle (that's a sharp object with a point)

parts.note: a pin is a small sharp object
E (east) is a compass point

explanation.surface: Tracing where a needle came from, with a pedantic aside about sharp points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needle' suggests sewing, but it is a conifer leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Conifer needles are the leaves of this evergreen tree, so it is where the needle came from.

clue.text: A lot above your head

parts.note: sounds like too much to understand, but a lot is a plot of land, here on top of a building

explanation.surface: Something that is a lot above your head, too much to grasp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot' means a plot of ground, not 'a great deal'.
explanation.definitionFit: A planted area on top of a building is a plot of ground overhead.

clue.text: Career medic can cover the whole round

indicators.note: a medic who can cover something goes around it, so the doctor's letters enclose the rest

parts.note: GP, general practitioner, is a family doctor
the whole means all of it
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A career doctor can cover the whole of a round of calls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' is a verb, to rush along headlong.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush along at speed, as a horse does at full pace.

clue.text: Abominable flu spreading after heat wave

indicators.note: after places the reworked flu behind the reworked heat
the word heat is set in motion like a wave, its letters rearranged
flu spreading has its letters scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A nasty flu epidemic spreading in the wake of a heatwave.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams: 'wave' shuffles HEAT into HATE, and 'spreading' shuffles FLU into FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Abominable and this word are synonyms meaning detestable or loathsome.

clue.text: Gosh, are they celebrating the death of a baddie?

definitions.meaning: gosh is an exclamation of surprise or exasperation

definitions.text: are they celebrating the death of a baddie?
definitions.meaning: pictures bells rung in the underworld to welcome a villain

explanation.surface: An exclamation, then a joking question about bells rung when a villain dies.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mild exclamation like gosh; taken literally it means the bells of the underworld.

clue.text: When it's pouring, can you look forward to getting a lift?

definitions.text: When it's pouring, can you look forward to getting a lift?

parts.words: When it's pouring, can you look forward to getting a lift?
parts.note: sounds like rain and a car ride, but means a mixer being poured, which lifts the spirits

explanation.surface: On a rainy day, can you hope someone will drive you home?
explanation.walkthrough: 'pouring' suggests rain and 'lift' a car ride; both belong to drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is a restorative pick-me-up, and this fizzy mixer is poured into gin.

clue.text: Ruled out a denial, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things backwards, so the remaining letters are read right to left
out means the word a is left out of denial

explanation.surface: Having reflected, someone decides that issuing a denial is ruled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes A from DENIAL, leaving DENIL, which 'on reflection' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruled paper has printed lines on it, so ruled is a synonym here.

clue.text: Learns to edit on a magazine

indicators.note: to edit something is to rework it, so the letters of learns and a are reordered

explanation.surface: A trainee learns to edit on a magazine's staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'magazine' suggests a publication; it is a store for weapons and ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine in the military sense is a store of arms, which is what an arsenal is.

clue.text: While protecting male's little bits

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping around, so the word for while goes around the male

parts.note: as can mean while, as in 'as I was walking'
a tom is a male animal, especially a cat

explanation.surface: Something protecting a man's private parts.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the tiniest particles of matter, so very small bits.

clue.text: Tears caused by quarrels

definitions.meaning: tears here are rips or splits in something
quarrels are breaks in relations between people

explanation.surface: Crying brought on by arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both physical splits or cracks and breaches in friendship.

clue.text: A diminutive fish

definitions.meaning: a diminutive is a word ending that makes something smaller, as in duckling or gosling
a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A tiny fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix forms small versions (duckling); it is also a long cod-like sea fish.

clue.text: Fur ball pet swallowed

indicators.note: a pet that swallowed something has it inside, so the ball goes within

parts.note: a cat is a common household pet
O is shaped like a ball

explanation.surface: A pet swallowed a furball.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's fur is its coat, its covering of hair.

clue.text: Gives the impression to go out with Miss would be 'too much'

parts.note: to see someone is to date or go out with them

indicators.note: the word is in Miss counts as too much and is cut, leaving the title Ms

explanation.surface: Going out with a young lady seems excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would be too much' removes IS from MISS to give MS.
explanation.definitionFit: If something gives the impression of being so, it appears or looks that way.

clue.text: No seats left for 'Betrayal'

definitions.meaning: an event where every ticket has gone
betrayal is selling out one's principles or friends

explanation.surface: A production of a play called Betrayal plays to a full house.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means both a fully booked show and a treacherous abandonment of one's side.

clue.text: Commute from close to the centre of Castlebar

parts.note: to close is to shut

indicators.note: the centre of the town name Castlebar is its middle three letters

explanation.surface: Commuting from near the middle of Castlebar, a town in County Mayo, Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To shuttle is to travel to and fro regularly, as commuters do.

clue.text: Get ahead or follow on

definitions.meaning: get ahead means prosper or do well
follow on means come after, take over from

explanation.surface: Advice to get ahead or else follow behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is one sense; the other is to come after, as an heir takes a throne.

clue.text: Points out other amendments in contract

indicators.note: points out means the points sit outside, around the rest

parts.note: S and N, south and north, are compass points

indicators.note: amendments change the word other, rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: A lawyer points out other amendments in a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like the legal document of the surface, but it is a verb, to make smaller; 'Points out' means the compass points go outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract something is to make it smaller or briefer.

clue.text: Back he goes inside to try again

indicators.note: goes inside means the word he is placed within the word for back

parts.note: the rear is the back of something

explanation.surface: He goes back inside to have another go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a reversal signal; it is REAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that tries a case again hears it a second time, a legal sense.

clue.text: Hard-wearing coat for a nipper

parts.note: sounds like a sturdy jacket for a child, but the nipper is a tooth and the coat its glossy outer layer

explanation.surface: A tough jacket bought for a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nipper' is British slang for a child, but here it is a tooth, which nips.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard outer layer covering a tooth is a durable glossy coating.

clue.text: When it comes to hearing, the very top is canine

indicators.note: when heard rather than read, the word for the very top gives the entry

parts.note: a peak is the summit, the very top

explanation.surface: Where hearing is concerned, the top performer is a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pekingese, a small Chinese lapdog breed, is a canine.

clue.text: Cut back to ball game

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is written backwards

parts.note: to lop is to cut off, as with branches
O is shaped like a ball

explanation.surface: Cutting back to a ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball game' looks like the definition, but only 'game' is: 'ball' is O.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo is a team sport played on horseback with mallets.

clue.text: 'With one's best behind one' is going too far

definitions.meaning: literally past one's peak, as in having gone beyond the summit
going too far means excessive, exaggerated

explanation.surface: Saying someone is past their best is going too far.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally beyond the summit, the phrase also means excessive or outrageous.

clue.text: Romanced in song

definitions.meaning: to romance is to tell fanciful, untrue stories
a German art song of the Romantic era

explanation.surface: Wooed someone through a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Romanced can mean told falsehoods; the word is also German for an art song, as by Schubert.

clue.text: They could get to read clippings a long time ago

indicators.note: clippings are cut-up pieces, so the letters of to read are chopped and reordered

explanation.surface: People could read old newspaper clippings from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clippings' shuffles TO READ into EAR DOT, after THEY.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a British idiom for a very long time ago, as if from the beginning of time.
